learn.hook: Seven giant pieces of land, and you live on the biggest one. Can you guess which?
points: A continent is a very large, continuous mass of land. There are seven continents.
From largest to smallest: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia.
Asia is the largest continent, and India is in Asia. Australia is the smallest and is also called an island continent.
Europe and Asia are joined together as one landmass (Eurasia); the Ural Mountains are often taken as the line between them.
Antarctica, around the South Pole, is covered with thick ice. It has no permanent towns, only research stations; India's stations there are Maitri and Bharati.

example.q: Rohan says, 'Australia is a country, so it can't be a continent.' Is he right?
steps: It is also a large landmass surrounded by water on all sides.
So it is counted as a continent, the smallest one, called an island continent.
example.answer: No. Australia is both a country and the smallest continent.

learn.reallife: When you watch a cricket match between India and Australia, the two teams come from two different continents: Asia and Australia!

quiz.q: How many continents are there on the Earth?
quiz.explain: The seven continents are Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe and Australia.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the number of continents with the number of oceans

quiz.q: Which is the largest continent?
quiz.explain: Asia is the largest continent in both area and number of people.
quiz.mistake: Thinks Africa is the largest because it looks big on maps

quiz.q: Which is the smallest continent?
quiz.explain: Australia is the smallest continent; Europe is the second smallest.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up Europe and Australia

quiz.q: On which continent is India located?
quiz.explain: India is in the southern part of Asia.
quiz.mistake: Does not know which continent India belongs to

quiz.q: Which continent is almost completely covered with thick ice?
quiz.explain: Antarctica lies around the South Pole and is covered by a huge ice sheet.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the Arctic region with the continent of Antarctica

quiz.q: What are the names of India's research stations in Antarctica?
quiz.explain: India runs the research stations Maitri and Bharati in Antarctica to study ice, weather and life there.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up research stations with space missions

quiz.q: Which mountains are often taken as the dividing line between Europe and Asia?
quiz.explain: Europe and Asia form one landmass; the Ural Mountains are usually used to mark the boundary.
quiz.mistake: Picks a well-known mountain range without checking where it is

quiz.q: Why is Australia called an island continent?
options: It is a continent surrounded by water on all sides
It has many tiny islands only
quiz.explain: An island is land surrounded by water; Australia is a whole continent like that.
quiz.mistake: Misunderstands the meaning of 'island'

teach.ask: Gappu wants to fly around the world. 'How many big pieces of land will I see? Which is the biggest?'
teach.praise: Hooray! Seven continents: Asia is the biggest and Australia is the smallest. I live in Asia too!
teach.nudge: How many continents are there, and which one is the biggest and which one the smallest?

learn.hook: If you could swim from Chennai going east, which ocean would you be in? Let's explore the oceans!
points: There are five oceans: the Pacific, the Atlantic, the Indian, the Southern and the Arctic.
The Pacific Ocean is the largest and the deepest ocean. Its deepest part is the Mariana Trench.
The Atlantic Ocean is the second largest and is shaped somewhat like the letter S.
The Indian Ocean is the only ocean named after a country: India. It lies south of India.
The Southern Ocean surrounds Antarctica, and the Arctic Ocean, the smallest, lies around the North Pole.

example.q: Which ocean would a ship from Kochi first sail into?
steps: Kochi is on the coast of Kerala, on the Arabian Sea.
The Arabian Sea is a part of the Indian Ocean.
So the ship sails into the Indian Ocean.

learn.reallife: The fish you eat in coastal cities like Kochi, Visakhapatnam and Mumbai come from the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal, both parts of the Indian Ocean.

quiz.q: How many oceans are there?
quiz.explain: The five oceans are the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the number of oceans with the number of continents

quiz.q: Which is the largest and deepest ocean?
quiz.explain: The Pacific is the biggest ocean and has the deepest place on Earth, the Mariana Trench.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the Atlantic is the largest

quiz.q: Which ocean is named after a country?
quiz.explain: The Indian Ocean is named after India, the only ocean named after a country.
quiz.mistake: Does not know how the Indian Ocean got its name

quiz.q: Which is the smallest ocean?
quiz.explain: The Arctic Ocean around the North Pole is the smallest ocean.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the Arctic and the Southern Ocean

quiz.q: Which ocean surrounds the continent of Antarctica?
quiz.explain: The Southern Ocean flows all around Antarctica.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the Arctic Ocean is at the South Pole

quiz.q: The Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal are parts of which ocean?
quiz.explain: Both seas lie on either side of peninsular India and are parts of the Indian Ocean.
quiz.mistake: Does not link nearby seas to their ocean

quiz.q: Where is the Mariana Trench, the deepest known place on Earth?
quiz.explain: The Mariana Trench is in the western Pacific Ocean.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the deepest place with the highest place

quiz.q: Which is the second largest ocean?
quiz.explain: After the Pacific, the Atlantic is the largest ocean.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the Indian Ocean is second largest

teach.ask: Gappu sees lots of blue on the globe. 'Is all this water one big ocean? Which part is near India?'
teach.praise: Splash! There are five oceans. The Pacific is the biggest, the Arctic is the smallest, and the Indian Ocean is right next to India!
teach.nudge: How many oceans are there, and which one is close to India?

learn.hook: Why do astronauts call the Earth the 'Blue Planet'? Look at how much water it has!
points: About 71% of the Earth's surface is covered with water and only about 29% is land.
About 97% of all the Earth's water is salty ocean water. Less than 3% is fresh water, and most of that is frozen as ice and glaciers.
The Northern Hemisphere has much more land than the Southern Hemisphere, which is mostly water.

Ocean water keeps moving: waves are mostly made by wind, tides are the regular rise and fall of the sea caused mainly by the pull of the Moon (and the Sun), and currents are large streams of water flowing in the oceans.
Oceans give us fish, salt and sea routes for ships, and they help control the Earth's climate.

example.q: Out of every 100 parts of the Earth's surface, about 71 are water. How many parts are land?

learn.reallife: Salt from the sea is made by drying seawater in shallow pans along the coasts of Gujarat and Tamil Nadu.

quiz.q: About what percentage of the Earth's surface is covered by water?
quiz.explain: Water covers about 71% of the surface, which is why the Earth looks blue from space.
quiz.mistake: Swaps the land and water percentages

quiz.q: About what percentage of the Earth's surface is land?
quiz.explain: Land covers only about 29% of the surface (100 − 71 = 29).
quiz.mistake: Swaps the land and water percentages

quiz.q: Why is the Earth called the 'Blue Planet'?
options: Its sky is blue at night
Most of its surface is covered by water
It is covered with blue rocks
quiz.explain: From space, the large oceans make the Earth look blue.
quiz.mistake: Links the name to the sky instead of the oceans

quiz.q: Where is most of the Earth's fresh water found?
quiz.explain: Less than 3% of Earth's water is fresh, and most of it is locked up as ice and glaciers.
quiz.mistake: Thinks rivers hold most of the fresh water

quiz.q: What mainly causes tides in the sea?
options: The pull of the Moon and the Sun
quiz.explain: The gravity of the Moon (and the Sun) pulls on ocean water, making the sea rise and fall.
quiz.mistake: Confuses tides with waves made by wind

quiz.q: What mainly makes waves on the ocean surface?
quiz.explain: Wind blowing over the water pushes it up into waves.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up waves and tides

quiz.q: Which hemisphere has more land?
quiz.explain: Most continents lie largely north of the Equator, so the Northern Hemisphere has more land.
quiz.mistake: Assumes land is spread equally

quiz.q: What are ocean currents?
options: Large streams of water flowing in the oceans
quiz.explain: Currents are like rivers within the ocean; some are warm and some are cold.
quiz.mistake: Confuses currents with waves

teach.ask: Gappu asks, 'If the Earth has so much water, why do we have to save water at home?'
teach.praise: Oh! Most water is salty ocean water, and the little fresh water there is, is mostly ice. So I must save every drop!
teach.nudge: Is most of the Earth's water fit to drink? Where is the fresh water?
